summary: The latest in blockchain tech upgrades, funding announcements and deals. For the period of Aug. 22-28.
title: Protocol Village: Sony-Backed Soneium Blockchain Launches Testnet, Peaq Powers Drone Network
content: Sony Group's blockchain joint venture with Startale Labs, Sony Block Solutions Labs (Sony BSL), launched the “Soneium Minato” public testnet, alongside an ambitious developer incubation program, "Soneium Spark." According to the team: "This dual initiative marks a significant milestone in Sony Group's entry in Web3, poised to catalyze ecosystem growth and accelerate adoption by leveraging its vast global reach and technological expertise across entertainment, gaming and consumer electronics sectors." The move comes a week after the pioneering electronics giant unveiled the plans to erect a layer-2 network atop Ethereum called Soneium, using technology from Optimism's OP Stack.

Parallel execution has arrived on Starknet with the 'Bolt' upgrade, expanding the Ethereum layer-2 blockchain's capacity "by enabling independent transactions to be executed simultaneously," according to the team: "The network is the first layer 2 to have 'megastore capabilities,' with the sequencer now able to execute multiple transactions in parallel. The introduction of Parallel Execution is part of the network's upgrade to version 13.2, which also includes Block Packing, a feature that makes use of every last bit of block space and will reduce confirmation time to two seconds — exactly what devs and users want from Starknet." {{STARK}}

Hyperway, described as a "decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) of community-owned ground relays for ensuring fast data exchange between delivery drones and ground control centers," is working with the layer-1 blockchain peaq for certain functionality, according to a blog post published Wednesday. The peaq team wrote in a message that "Hyperway is building a DePIN of community-owned ground-based stations serving drones, air taxis, autonomous cargo ships and other transport. It has partnered with four Asian governments (Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Japan) and signed a major agreement with the Malaysian state of Sabah to support cargo drone operations in agriculture." The blog post elaborated that "as part of the integration with peaq, Hyperway will build the software needed to connect 5G and satellite ground relays with peaq. It will also build the smart contracts rewarding the owners of such stations with tokens based on how much bandwidth the drones have used up. It will also integrate peaq-compatible digital wallets into the DePIN and run a restricted public trial involving real-world drone flights powered by its DePIN."

BNB Chain has launched BNB Chain Bridge. According to the team: "Developed with Celer, deBridge, and Stargate, BNB Chain Bridge will enhance cross-chain interoperability, liquidity, and user experience on BNB Chain. The key takeaways:

Lemniscap, a Cayman Islands-headquartered investment firm, said it raised a $70 million fund to back early stage Web3 projects. The fund will focus on projects in the Bitcoin ecosystem, reflecting a trend of the past 18 months, whereby developers have sought to introduce to the world's oldest blockchain utility that is more commonly associated with the likes of the Ethereum network. Lemniscap is targeting zero-knowledge infrastructure, consumer applications and decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN), according to an emailed announcement on Wednesday.

Mezo, describing itself as an "economic layer built by Bitcoin venture studio Thesis," and fellow project Acre, "the BTC-in-BTC-out staking platform," have launched stBTC, "the first liquid, yield-bearing Bitcoin product built on tBTC," according to the team: "By generating yield on Mezo users’ locked assets, stBTC boosts liquidity for putting Bitcoin to work on popular DeFi platforms including Curve. StBTC helps secure the BitcoinFi ecosystem amid tBTC’s traction as WBTC faces an uncertain future. It further strengthens Mezo's position as a top Bitcoin L2 with $165M in TVL and 16K total depositors on its platform to date."

FIRST IN PROTOCOL VILLAGE: Hinkal, an institutional self-custodial protocol designed for cross-chain shared privacy, announced the formation of its Board of Curators, which includes leading trading firms such as Re7 Labs, Dialectic, Theia, Agnostic and Aquanow "to bring privacy to on-chain dApps." According to the team: "These firms will participate in the dApp selection and whitelisting process, ensuring that only high-quality applications can enable private and compliant transactions on the platform. This initiative aims to enhance privacy and security in decentralized finance (DeFi) by integrating Hinkal’s privacy SDK, allowing for private on-chain liquidity and safeguarding user strategies." Hinkal is currently deployed on the Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche and Blast mainnets.

Aethir, a leading provider of enterprise-grade GPUs-as-a-service, has partnered with Auros, a top crypto-native algorithmic trading firm, "to advance on-chain payments and enhance the use of ATH token transactions for compute credits," according to the team: "By integrating Auros’s technology, Aethir will boost transparency and efficiency in financial transactions, enabling enterprise clients across industries like telecommunications, gaming and AI to seamlessly access decentralized compute services. All transactions will be executed on-chain, ensuring visibility, trust, and optimal value for stakeholders."

DecideAI, a Web3 company focused on creating AI-based large language models (LLMs), announced the launch of its full on-chain implementation of the GPT-2 LLM on the Internet Computer (ICP) blockchain, powered by its native DCD token. According to the team: "This marks a significant milestone in the fusion of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence, showcasing the Internet Computer's unique capabilities in supporting complex, compute-intensive applications."

Creditcoin, a proof-of-stake blockchain project for real-world assets such as stocks, bonds and real estate (RWAs) and aiming to connect emerging markets, is launching its EVM-compatible mainnet, enabling developers to build dApps seamlessly. According to the team: "This upgrade streamlines dApp migration from Ethereum and enhances cross-chain interactions via Creditcoin's Universal Smart Contract layer, eliminating traditional bridging. Creditcoin also introduces CreditWallet, designed to interact with multiple blockchain ecosystems and provide a superior user experience. This complements Creditcoin’s original chain on Substrate, focused on helping financial institutions build on-chain credit reputations."

Protocol Village is a regular feature of The Protocol, our weekly newsletter exploring the tech behind crypto, one block at a time. Sign up here to get it in your inbox every Wednesday. Project teams can submit updates here. For previous versions of Protocol Village, please go here.

Tonkeeper, a wallet for the TON blockchain, announced the launch of its dApp browser in Telegram. According to the team: "Integrated into the Tonkeeper wallet, the browser provides a gateway to exploring the best decentralized applications available within the growing TON ecosystem. Launch partners whose dApps are integrated into the Tonkeeper browser include leading DEX, which makes it easy to swap hundreds of TON assets; eSIM provider Ton Mobile, which offers cellular services in more than 150 countries; and Wizzwoods, the first Pixel Farm game that integrates interchain capabilities with a SoFi twist."

WeaveVM, describing itself as a "hyperscalable EVM network designed for unparalleled storage and high-throughput data availability (DA)," officially launched its Alphanet V0.1.0. According to the team: "Developed by Decent Land Labs, this solution addresses challenges in the blockchain industry, including the EVM storage bottleneck and the inefficiencies of temporary DA. WeaveVM is the only EVM chain using Arweave for storage, ensuring long-term data security and accessibility. WeaveVM offers a high-performance network, featuring 1 gigagas per second capacity, 48,000 transactions per second (TPS), and throughput exceeding 125MB/s."

Bluwhale, an AI Web3 start-up connecting enterprises to consenting wallet holders and enabling digital profile monetization, announced the launch of a mobile web app "for a vastly simplified process of contributing/verifying data and even operating nodes." According to the team, the app "enables one-click node sale and operation, giving retail users access to the wave of node sales as well as all the benefits of node sale participation. Bluwhale is also launching the Node Alliance to give partners the same capabilities, and their communities the same benefits. Saltwater Games and Revolving Games are the first Alliance partners."

KOR Protocol, backed by Animoca Brands, introduced KOR Player, a platform that lets developers integrate licensed music and IP-based assets into their ecosystems, addressing copyright challenges. According to the team: "Co-founded by industry leaders like deadmau5, KOR Player features tools like the IP Vault for artist uploads and an AI engine that provides access to a growing sound library. Developers can integrate this as an SDK for seamless music and IP-based experiences. The platform ensures on-chain royalties for artists and simplifies rights management, allowing developers to create without licensing worries."

Masa, a decentralized AI network where people earn by contributing data, announced that its Subnet 42 is now fully integrated into Bittensor’s neural network and is live on mainnet. According to the team: "The Masa Bittensor Subnet will be joined by nine Genesis Institutional Validator Partners including Foundry, Republic, Nocturnal Labs, Luganodes, P2P, Animoca, DSRV, Crypto Times and InfStone. Masa’s AI data subnet, reached its full miner capacity in the first week, and was over capacity by 192% during its 6-week incentivized testnet."

RDX Works, developer of the Radix public ledger, announced the development of Flash Liquidity, "a DeFi liquidity solution aimed at solving DeFi’s challenge of fragmented liquidity by aggregating liquidity into a single ecosystem." According to the team: "By allowing market makers to offer liquidity without requiring upfront inventory on Radix, Flash Liquidity unlocks deeper and more efficient markets, with liquidity and asset availability comparable to centralized exchanges but all within a non-custodial DeFi setting. Flash Liquidity is being built in collaboration with Keyrock, G-20, Portofino and Instabridge."

Syndicate, building blockchain infrastructure including the "Transaction Cloud" designed to make it easier and cheaper for developers to launch applications and layers on Ethereum-compatible blockchains, announced the Metabased initiative. According to the team, it's a "community of organizations leading the development and decentralization of the next layer of Ethereum. Our initial cohort of 15+ orgs will collaborate and accelerate the adoption of decentralized community roll-ups at scale."

Sorella Labs, an Ethereum-focused developer that says it's "building tools to protect DeFi liquidity providers from the multi-billion dollar arbitrage and extraction industry and create a fairer and more efficient trading environment," announced a $7.5 million seed round led by Paradigm. According to the team: "They also announced 1) Brontes, an open-source MEV explorer for Ethereum and 2) Angstrom, an upcoming Uniswap V4 hook that protects both LPs and swappers, paving the way for sustainable, decentralized, and welfare-maximizing decentralized exchanges."

RepubliK, an AI-powered, blockchain-based SocialFi platform, launched Creator STOX on the STOX Market, "transforming social media monetization by allowing fans to support creators directly using RPK Tokens on Arbitrum." According to the team: "With over 200 STOXs minted, 2.33 million RPK locked, and 3,363 trades facilitated, the platform is rapidly growing. Creator STOX pools distribute fees from fan subscriptions and token-gated chats, fueled by current STOX influencers' combined social following of 12.8 million across X, Instagram, and TikTok."

A collective group of industry leaders, including Alluvial, Coinbase, Aon, Blockdaemon, Chainproof, DV Labs, Eigen Labs, Figment, Galaxy, Nexus Mutual and others, launched the Node Operator Risk Standard (NORS) certification, a first-of-its-kind certification designed for Ethereum node operator risk management. NORS sets a new benchmark for operational security and risk management within the Ethereum ecosystem. The introduction of NORS Certification makes institutional-grade trust for Ethereum staking achievable, simplifying the due diligence process for banks and large institutions.

Gameplay Galaxy, creators of the Trial Xtreme series with over 300 million downloads, secured an additional $11 million in seed funding, totaling $24 million. According to the team: "Led by Blockchain Capital and Merit Circle, the investment supports their vision for a Web3 competitive gaming ecosystem. Trial Xtreme Freedom aims to transition from Free-to-Play to Web3 by introducing features like track ownership and token earning. The funds will be used to accelerate product development, expand the team, and enhance go-to-market strategies, positioning the company to lead in the Web3 gaming space."

SOON (Solana Optimistic Network), describing itself as a "rollup stack powered by decoupled SVM" and built on Optimism's OP Stack, has successfully raised a co-builder round from Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko, Solana Foundation's Lily Liu, Coinbase Ventures's Jonathan King, Celestia's Mustafa Al-Bassam and other prominent builders. According to the team: "SOON Stack is poised to be the highest throughput rollup stack that allows for settlement on any layer 1, using the Solana Virtual Machine as the execution layer. This will offer scalability and efficiency for dApps on any L1 blockchain outside of Solana, exceeding the capabilities of any existing SVM project." The amount of the fundraise wasn't disclosed.

Space and Time (SxT), a blockchain-native data warehouse that incorporates artificial intelligence (AI) tools to build applications using its data, has raised $20 million in Series A funding. The funding round, which takes SxT's total backing to $50 million, was led by Framework Ventures, Lightspeed Faction, Arrington Capital and Hivemind Capital, according to an emailed announcement on Tuesday.

RootstockLabs, the developer behind the Ethereum EVM-compatible Bitcoin sidechain Rootstock, said it will participate as a key sponsor in ETHOnline 2024, a hackathon for the crypto space taking place Aug. 26 to Sept. 13, where a prize pool of $225,000 is to be won. According to the team, RootstockLabs will be "supporting participating DeFi developers and providing three prizes totaling $10,000 for the best project specifically built for the Rootstock platform during this event. ETH Online 2024 is the latest in a string of hackathons that Rootstock has been a part of in 2024, with prior events including Bitcoin Startup Lab Hackathon, EasyA Hackathon at Consensus 2024, Taikai's Bitcoin Meets Solidity Hackathon and the Ethereum Community Conference."

Radix, a distributed ledger project built around native assets known as "resources," has announced the planned creation of the 1.5 billion XRD ($37 million) Endowment Fund. According to the team: "The fund is intended to support long term ecosystem growth while securing financial support for the entities involved in the development and growth of the Radix platform and ecosystem. The process of selecting an institution to manage the fund – one requirement is that it have a balance sheet in excess of $1 billion in crypto – is underway. The selected partner will use Copper Custody, a regulated crypto custodian, to hold the XRD assets, and Twinstake, to provide the staking infrastructure where tokens may be deployed and staked as part of the overall strategy." (XRD)

Curvance, a modular protocol for optimized liquidity management, launched their public testnet on Ethereum's Sepolia, Arbitrum's Sepolia and Berachain's bArtio V2. According to the team: "Public testnet is the final chance to submit feedback and, most importantly, earn some coveted Bytes. Public testers in the Curvance testnet can collect up to 300 Bytes."

Fetch.ai, creating an agentic framework for autonomous digital ecosystems and a founding member of the Artificial Superintelligence Alliance, announced the launch of its Innovation Lab in San Francisco. According to the team: "This new center will drive the development of AI agent solutions that provide real value to businesses and consumers globally. To boost innovation in this area, Fetch.ai will invest $10 million annually to support projects focused on building AI agent solutions using its technology stack."

Sony, the Japanese electronics giant famous for developing the Betamax and Walkman in the 1970s, is now starting its own blockchain. Sony Block Solutions Labs, a joint project between Sony Group and Singapore-based Startale Labs, said Friday it's coming out with a new layer-2 network atop the Ethereum blockchain called Soneium. It will be built using the Optimism blockchain ecosystem’s OP Stack.

NEAR Protocol has deployed a major upgrade known as "Nightshade 2.0" on its main network, designed to improve the scalability and usability of the blockchain. New features include "stateless validation," a concept that Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has written about extensively, according to a press release from the NEAR Foundation, which supports the blockchain.

Appchain protocol Tanssi, historically focused on the Polkadot blockchain, is expanding to Ethereum with Symbiotic, a restaking protocol. According to the team, the effort could set "a new standard for the rapid launch of decentralized networks, aka Actively Validated Services (AVSs). What usually takes months can be done in minutes, allowing developers to deploy highly customizable and decentralized networks, with Ethereum’s robust security."

SatLayer has raised $8 million in pre-seed funding, led by Hack VC and Castle Island Ventures, "to expand Bitcoin as a universal security layer," according to the team: "Founded by MIT, Y Combinator, and Stanford alumni, SatLayer leverages Babylon Chain’s Proof of Stake to secure Actively Validated Services via BTC staking. 'We're excited for SatLayer’s launch on Babylon and its impact on BTC-secured AVSs,' said Fisher Yu, Babylon’s co-founder and CTO. Users can stake Bitcoin on Babylon, restake liquid staking tokens (LST) through platforms like Lombard, PumpBTC and PStake on SatLayer, and earn rewards."

The founders of VitaDAO, a Web3 community devoted to longevity health research and products, launched BIO, a "new protocol enabling global communities of patients, scientists and biotech builders to collectively fund and commercialize new therapeutics," according to the team: "Revenue from new therapeutics flow back into the BIO Network, creating value for network participants. BIO completed the first round of its TGE, raising $6.2 in a public sale, with participation from VCs like Zee Prime, 1kx ID Theory. Details on the second round of BIO’s TGE will be announced soon." According to the project documentation: "BioDAOs raise funding via token sales, and use their treasuries to back and develop biotech projects related to their mission, creating shared IP ownership between their members. BioDAOs use Molecule's on-chain IP framework to own, license, and transact in intellectual property generated from the projects they support."

Ark Labs, building a Bitcoin layer-2 network, has secured $2.5 million in pre-seed funding led by Draper Associates, with backing from Fulgur Ventures, Axiom Capital and angel investor Stephen Cole. According to the team: "This funding will advance Ark Labs’ work on seamless, scalable Bitcoin payments via the Ark protocol. Signups are open for the Ark Node beta, a user-friendly Lightning Network wallet. Ark Labs is seeking talent, developers, and partners to join its mission to revolutionize global payments."

Zellic, a provider of security audits in the blockchain industry, announced its acquisition of Code4rena, a project for competitive audits, claiming "the largest collection of security researchers in the space." According to the team "This strategic move marks Zellic's first acquisition and will enable both companies to offer clients a new level of deeply comprehensive security review, Audits+. Code4rena will continue to operate as its own business under its original brand, with its existing team and leadership intact."

Stork Network, a provider of pricing oracles across several asset classes, announced that it has raised $4.705 million in seed funding. According to the team: "This fundraising round is co-led by Lightspeed Faction and Lattice, with participation from CMS and Wintermute Ventures. The funds will be used to expand Stork Network's product suite including building out and bringing to market the Open Data Market. Meredith Pitkoff, co-founder at Stork Network.

SwapKit.dev, a provider of cross-chain infrastructure solutions, announced an integration with BitPay, the Bitcoin and cryptocurrency payment processor. According to the team: "This integration will empower BitPay users to unlock a wider range of digital assets, leveraging SwapKit to access cross-chain liquidity via THORChain for seamless in-wallet exchange of diverse cryptocurrencies. This partnership will provide significant benefits for Bitpay users, including:

PROTOCOL VILLAGE EXCLUSIVE: Credbull, which in April launched what it described as the "first licensed on-chain private credit fund" on the Polygon PoS blockchain, announced a $5.2 million funding round led by GnosisVC, with strategic participation from Outlier Ventures, HODL Ventures, XBTO, LucidBlue Ventures, CryptoHedge, Marcello Mari (SingularityDAO) and others. According to the team, "Credbull aims to democratize private credit RWA investments by connecting traditional finance with Web3."

Aave, the biggest DeFi lending protocol with a total value locked of $11.9 billion, announced the launch of Aave V3 on Era Mainnet, powered by ZKsync. According to the team, "Aave can access advanced ZK tech with low-cost transactions while deriving security from ETH with cryptographic validity proofs." Chainlink, the blockchain oracle project, "will provide secure and reliable price feeds." Aave founder Stani Kulechov said in a statement relayed by a spokesperson for the project: "Era Mainnet offers the highest level of scalability and performance and with zero knowledge proofs, the opportunity to add privacy capabilities and additional security for users and institutions. Additionally, the Elastic Chain ecosystem can expand to accommodate various institutional use cases while ensuring scalability.” (AAVE) {{ZK}}

Chronicle, which was the first oracle on Ethereum and is currently the sole securer of MakerDAO, has launched its RWA Oracle via an integration with M^0, "an on-chain protocol that allows multiple Minters to issue a fully fungible cryptodollar called $M." According to the team: "In this collaboration, Chronicle serves as an independent validator, verifying M^0’s collateral balances. As a result of its integration with M^0, Chronicle is permissioned by the protocol’s governance to provide timely information on the off-chain collateral being used by Minters to generate $M, ensuring the integrity and reliability of the $M cryptodollar."

Legion, describing itself as a "merit-based ICO platform," has emerged from stealth and announced a $2 million raise from founders, accelerators and angels. Backers include Cyber Fund, AllianceDAO, Delphi Labs, CoinGecko, Mike Dudas, Alex Svanevik, Peter Smith, Maggie Love, Jon Wu, Ryan Watkins and LongHash. According to the team: "The platform plans to become MiCA compliant and provide investment access to non-accredited investors. By ranking investors by merit (on-chain and off-chain reputation), rather than net-wealth, Legion says teams can build higher quality communities, and short-term holders are disincentivized."

BNB Chain has announced that four top-performing projects from Season 7 of its MVB program – an accelerator designed to drive growth within the BNB Chain ecosystem – have received investment from Binance Labs. The selected projects include:

Myco.io, a Web3 streaming platform, announced a strategic partnership with Aptos Foundation to ship content on the Aptos blockchain. According to the team: "The collaboration will focus around technical integration, developing builder resources and a mutual commitment to advancing Web3 technologies and delivering next-generation, decentralized digital streaming experiences." (APT)

Aave, which had already deployed on the Ethereum layer-2 network Metis, has integrated METIS as collateral, "expanding asset management strategies for users," according to the team: "With a 30% LTV ratio, users can borrow assets based on their METIS holdings. This offers liquidity without selling METIS, access to various financial tools and benefits from faster, cheaper transactions on Metis compared to Ethereum mainnet."

Mira, a decentralized AI infrastructure platform, hired Ninad Naik, a former Uber executive, as chief product officer. According to the team: "In his new role, Ninad will spearhead product innovation, playing a crucial role in Mira’s mission to expand global AI access through decentralization. Ninad joins Mira from Uber, where he led the core marketplace product for Uber's food and grocery delivery business globally. Prior to Uber, Ninad has held multiple GM and product leadership roles at Amazon across its AI, hardware, and marketplace businesses."

Yonsei University's AI researchers will use Theta EdgeCloud to accelerate AI model training and inference for research in machine reasoning and data mining, according to the team: "Led by Professor Dongha Lee, the lab will develop advanced tools like a table reasoner and summarizer to extract implicit knowledge from tabular data. By utilizing Theta's scalable platform, the lab can reduce costs by more than 50% compared to traditional cloud services."

OORT, a cloud platform for decentralized AI, has partnered with the National Science Foundation's(NSF) eCAT (Electric, Connected, and Autonomous Technologies for Mobility) IUCRC research center. According to the team: "OORT, which provides a blockchain-based verification layer for data used by AI engines, will collaborate closely with leading institutions in this project including Wayne State University, Clarkson University, the University of North Texas, the University of Delaware and Oakland University. OORT will also work alongside companies including leading American Data Storage and Western Digital."

GaiaNet, a project for decentralized AI inferencing, is launching a global "Living Knowledge Systems Hackathon," which will run from Aug. 22 to Sept. 13. Registration began Aug. 19, 2024. According to the team: "The prize pool will include up to $50K in rewards. Winning participants will also be invited on an expense-paid trip to TOKEN2049 Singapore, where they will join the GaiaNet executive team at an exclusive launch party. The aim of the event is to build decentralized nodes, solve security vulnerabilities in centralized AI models and tackle issues like censorship, algorithmic bias and data privacy."
Edited by Bradley Keoun.
